Check for data loss after transformation and binding

Source: R/check_data_loss.R
check_data_loss.Rd

Compares a list of original (pre-dict_apply()) data frames against the master dataset produced by harm_bind_waves() to detect four classes of information loss: missing rows, dropped variables, new NA values introduced in mapped columns, and unexpected category collapse in factor variables. Run this after harm_bind_waves() and before assign_standard_labels().

Usage

check_data_loss(data_list, master, wb_path)

Arguments

data_list

A named list of data frames as passed to dict_init(), before dict_apply(). List names must match the wave labels used in the dictionary (e.g. list(w1 = ..., w2 = ...) corresponds to dictionary columns orig_w1, orig_w2).

master

A data frame or tibble, the output of harm_bind_waves(). Must contain a source_wave column.

wb_path

Character string. Path to the .xlsx dictionary file, used to read Variable_Map_Wide for name translation.

Value

If all checks pass, returns invisible(NULL) and prints a success message. If issues are found, emits a warning and returns a tibble of flagged rows with columns wave, target_name, check, before, after, delta, and status.

Examples

wave1 <- data.frame(id = c("alice", "bob"), gender = c("Female", "Male"))

dict_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  list(Variable_Map_Wide = data.frame(
    target_name = c("id", "gender"),
    orig_w1     = c("id", "gender")
  )),
  file = dict_path
)

master <- data.frame(
  id          = c("alice", "bob"),
  gender      = factor(c("1", "2")),
  source_wave = "w1"
)

check_data_loss(list(w1 = wave1), master, dict_path)
#> ✔ All transformation checks passed. No data loss detected.
